scope: preliminary verse-specific screening, not full verification
methodology: Qur'an 4:90 Arabic and English read on Quran.com; Deuteronomy 20:10-12 English New American Bible Revised Edition read at USCCB. Other verse summaries preliminary; no critical text or manuscript comparison. Generic motifs are not public sources.

verses.summary: Public profession of obedience followed by contrary private planning; God records it
Call to reflect on Qur'anic coherence rather than contradictions
Reports of security or fear should be referred to messenger and responsible authorities
Messenger urged to fight and encourage believers despite others' choices
Good intercession and bad intercession carry corresponding responsibility
Return a greeting with an equal or better greeting; divine accounting
Affirmation of divine oneness and certain resurrection
Disagreement about hypocrites and their responsibility for actions
Warning about alliance with opponents who reject faith, qualified by following verse
Exceptions for treaty-connected people and those who refrain from combat and offer peace

staged_candidates.relationship: contrast in conflict and peace terms
staged_candidates.similarity: Both discuss restraint or peace proposals amid hostilities.
staged_candidates.difference: Deuteronomy 20:10-12 concerns an attacking army's offer of terms to a city, potentially including forced labor, followed by siege if refused; Qur'an 4:90 exempts treaty-linked or noncombatant parties who refrain from fighting and offer peace. Different parties, conditions, and consequences.
staged_candidates.verification: English NABRE inspected, Qur'an Arabic and English inspected. Hebrew critical edition, textual variants, manuscript witnesses and scholarly interpretation not collated. Staged only.
